messages:
maya: quick follow-up on the subpage aliasing + coalescer RFC — want to lock down a few API boundaries before I start the refactor
kevin: tl;dr? what's 'subpage aliasing' in this context?
maya: short: let multiple tiny tensors share one pinned physical page by mapping distinct byte ranges as read-only/heavy-read views instead of separate allocations. reduces pin churn + PCIe copies for small convo batches.
li: sounds useful. how do we handle write semantics? copy-on-write?
maya: yeah COW for writes. plan is to detect when a view is promoted to mutable and then do a shallow copy into a new pinned page (async), update view mapping, and use a small fence for consistency.
sam: worried about race windows with in-flight kernels. what's the fence model?
maya: two parts: (1) CUDA stream quiesce for the tenant stream that caused the mutation, (2) an epoch seq on the allocator; other readers keep using old mapping until epoch advance. cheap metadata check in runtime.
kevin: allocator API changes? breaking?
maya: minimal surface: add AllocView handle and AllocView::promote(). Old alloc path stays. consumers can opt-in per-op via small flag: { view_allowed: true } in alloc hints.
li: how about telemetry? need to know how often we trigger COW and how much pin-savings we get.
maya: we'll add metrics: alloc_view_created, view_promoted (with size), pin_share_ratio, stale_view_lifetime. Also a histogram for COW latency.
mem-bot: CI: small test v1.2 failed on pinned_page_allocator_test::alias_overlap_case (request id 7c9) :warning:
kevin: good catch from CI. that test probably hits overlapping alias creation. we should hard-fail overlapping writable ranges at create time. readonly overlaps fine.
maya: agreed. runtime will check overlap table and reject if any existing writable mapping intersects requested range. reject policy returns EINVAL with a hint to allocate a dedicated page.
sam: what about fragmentation? if many small views anchor a page that is mostly free, coalescer should recycle pages by migrating live views to a new compact page and freeing the old one, right?
maya: yep — that's the coalescer background job. heuristic: when live_bytes < 30% and free runs across pages > 128KB, schedule compaction. migration uses pinned staging + peer-copy to move live slices out, update view metadata atomically.
li: can compaction be preempted if load spikes? we shouldn't block allocations.
maya: compaction is low-priority, preemptible. we use a token bucket tied to tenant SLOs; if tenant is backpressure-sensitive, coalescer backs off. also a global soft-cap for compaction bandwidth.
kevin: security/tenancy concern: view aliasing could expose memory across tenants if we make a bookkeeping mistake. how do we guard?
maya: strong checks: (1) views carry tenant id in the mapping metadata; (2) mmap ops validate tenant before granting a handle; (3) audit logs for every alias creation. plus unit tests for cross-tenant overlap attempts.
sam: edge case: pinned memory pressure + many small views -> fallback path. what's fallback?
maya: fallback is to allocate regular dedicated pinned page (no alias) or use host-staging page with faster NVMe-backed spill when pinned budget exceeded. we prefer dedicated page if small but hot writes expected.
kevin: any perf modelling yet? would like a microbenchmark for chat-style workload (many small <2KB tensors) vs baseline.
maya: I'm working on a synthetic harness — plan to measure throughput, PCIe writes, and tail-latency of small allocs. expecting ~25-40% pin reduction on chat-like traces.
li: can we support this in Private deploys (on-prem) where drivers vary?
maya: yes, feature gates. default off for legacy drivers; enable if driver reports unified pinned map and supports efficient peer-copy. detect at runtime.
kevin: would be good to have a short API sketch for SDK team so they can expose view_allowed hint.
maya: posted a tiny sketch here: https://internal.redwood/rfc/subpage-aliasing (WIP)
sam: ok next actions?
maya: (1) lock API surface (AllocView handle + promote) — i'll push a small PR with header-only changes, (2) add safety checks in pinned allocator for overlap + tenant id, (3) coalescer heuristics as a separate follow-up PR, (4) add unit tests and microbench harness.
kevin: +1 on the plan. please add mem-bot test that fuzzes overlapping ranges.
mem-bot: queued: add-fuzz-test-for-aliasing (job id 81234) :white_check_mark:
li: thanks — ping me when API PR is ready, i'll review the consistency/fence bits.
maya: thanks team. I'll open the PR later today and drop notes for SDK/console integration. :rocket:
